title: peer contentType CRLF panics blob_download_handler
description:
Trigger: peer sends Peer/deliver with attachment contentType containing CRLF (e.g. "application/octet-stream\r\nX-Evil: injected"). validate_attachments accepts it (checks only for '/' structure and length, not control chars). The value is stored in the attachments table. When the owner later requests GET /jmap/download/…, blob_download_handler reads content_type from DB and passes it to Response::builder().header(CONTENT_TYPE, content_type). The http crate's HeaderValue::from_str rejects CRLF, the builder returns Err, and the trailing .unwrap() panics. The tokio task for that connection terminates; the client gets a connection reset. The malicious blob is permanently undownloadable.

Fix: in validate_attachments, after the split_once('/') check, add: if a.content_type.bytes().any(|b| b < 0x20 || b == 0x7f) { return Err(...) }
